state: The tracking page sat frozen at 'label created' for nine straight days, and the linen blazer I'd ordered specifically for my sister's engagement dinner finally reached my door two full days after the dinner had already happened.

Nothing wrong with the actual robot dinosaur itself, mind you — no missing gears, no dead batteries, no factory defect to speak of. The trouble started before it ever reached us: the courier apparently used the box as a stepping stool, because it showed up with the roof caved in and one leg jutting clean through the cardboard. Impressive engineering, tragic handling. My daughter loves it anyway, dented skull and all.

My uncle always says good things come to those who wait, but even he'd have grumbled after our bookshelf spent three weeks bouncing between two regional hubs before it finally turned up on the porch, a full month later than promised.
I expected maybe a torn cover or a bent corner, nothing more; instead the box sat at the wrong address for two days in the rain before I tracked it down, and every page had warped.
The parcel arrived precisely on the date promised, the box unblemished and every corner intact; it is a pity, then, that the tennis racket within had a warped frame straight from the factory.

Somewhere between the warehouse and my apartment, this dresser apparently took a scenic tour through three different distribution centers, showing up on my stoop a full two weeks after the date I'd circled on the calendar.

So I ordered this building block set for my son's birthday like a month in advance because I know how these things go, and sure enough the courier tried to deliver it to a house four streets over even though I triple-checked the address at checkout, and by the time the neighbor finally tracked me down and dropped it off the party had already happened, so we did a cake-only celebration and handed him the blocks two days late while he kept asking where his present went.

Hi everyone! Just wanted to share my thoughts on this cardigan — the color is gorgeous and it's so soft, but I ordered a medium and it fits more like a small, especially through the shoulders. I ended up giving it to my sister since it was way too snug on me. Great material, just runs small, so maybe size up if you're in between!

I purchased this hardcover edition of 'The Quiet Orchard' as a birthday gift for my wife, who has long admired the author's earlier work, and I feel obliged to record my impressions in some detail. The volume itself is handsomely bound, with a cloth spine and a pleasant weight in the hand, and for that the publisher deserves credit. My reservations concern the contents rather than the container. The typesetting, regrettably, leaves something to be desired: the margins are uneven from chapter to chapter, and on no fewer than a dozen pages the font size appears to shrink without explanation, as though two different plates were used in the printing. More troubling still, the second half of the book contains a translation that reads rather stiffly compared with the first, suggesting a change of translator that was never disclosed. Several idioms are rendered so literally that their meaning is obscured entirely, and I found myself consulting the original language edition merely to confirm what a passage was meant to convey. The index, moreover, omits at least three names I specifically searched for, which for a work of this scholarly pretension strikes me as a genuine oversight. My wife, an exacting reader, noticed the same inconsistencies within the first evening and remarked that the publisher ought to have engaged a single proofreader throughout. I cannot in good conscience call this a poor book, for the writing itself remains as fine as ever, but the physical production and editorial oversight fall well short of what a reader of my vintage has come to expect from a house of this reputation.

Prior to placing this order, I reviewed the manufacturer's size chart and cross-referenced it against three prior purchases from the same brand, anticipating that the primary risk would be an inaccurate fit through the chest and shoulders given past experience with similarly cut jackets. That concern turned out to be unfounded: the garment, once it eventually reached me, matched the stated measurements within a few millimeters, and the stitching and fabric weight were exactly as specified in the product listing. The actual failure occurred entirely within the fulfillment chain. The order confirmation quoted a four-to-six business day window via a named carrier; instead, the tracking record shows the package was scanned into a facility eleven miles from my listed address, then re-routed twice through what appears to have been an automated sorting error, adding nine calendar days to the transit time. During that period, the carrier's own system marked the shipment as 'delivered' on day six, which was demonstrably false, since I was monitoring the porch camera continuously and no vehicle approached the property until day fifteen. I filed a support ticket referencing the discrepancy between the timestamp and the camera log, and the seller eventually confirmed that a routing label had been misapplied at the regional hub. Given that the jacket itself performed exactly as engineered, I have no complaint whatsoever about the product's construction or sizing. My assessment here concerns only the logistics failure: a false status update, a nine-day unexplained delay, and a routing error that required manual intervention to resolve. I would order the same garment again without hesitation, provided the carrier is changed.

I ordered a 27-inch monitor from this seller for a home office upgrade, selecting the seller's standard ground option with a stated transit window of three to five business days. The package did not arrive within that window. On day seven, the carrier's tracking page updated to 'exception, damaged in facility,' with no further detail. On day nine, after I contacted support, a second tracking number was issued, and the box that ultimately arrived on day thirteen showed a large tear along one seam, with packing peanuts spilling out onto my doorstep. Upon opening it, I found the monitor's outer casing cracked along the bottom edge and one corner of the screen visibly shattered, consistent with a significant impact during transit rather than any manufacturing defect. Photographs I took immediately after unboxing were submitted to support, along with the original history documenting the delay and the damage flag. The replacement unit, sent afterward via a different carrier, arrived intact within two days and functions correctly. For the record, the electronics themselves — controller board, panel, stand hinge — were sound in the replacement; the entire issue traced back to rough handling and an extended, unexplained delay in the original shipment.

I was so nervous this coffee table would get held up in transit like my last order from a different site, but nope — it actually showed up right on schedule, box in perfect shape! My only tiny gripe is that the finish felt a little rough on one corner, like it hadn't been sanded quite as smooth as the rest. Not a big deal, just wanted to mention it.

Okay so I love the color of this bookshelf, it's exactly the sage green I wanted, but two of the shelf pegs were bent at weird angles right out of the box and one shelf wobbles no matter how I adjust it. Kind of bummed because the design itself is really cute, I just wish the hardware quality matched it. Might order replacement pegs separately.

ok so the monstera itself is kinda underwhelming ngl, the leaves are this weird pale yellow color and it's WAY smaller than what the listing photos showed lol. like i get plants vary but this felt like false advertising tbh. no fenestrations either which was literally the whole reason i wanted this one. probably won't reorder from this specific listing again.

I want to walk through exactly what happened with this order, because I think the details matter: I placed the order for a pair of trail running shoes on a Monday, paid extra for two-day shipping, and received an email confirming dispatch that same evening. However, the package did not move from the origin facility for six full days, according to the carrier's own timestamped scan history, and when it finally did ship, it was routed to an entirely different zip code two towns over before someone corrected the address and forwarded it to me, ten days after the original promised date.

got this novel last week, cover looks nice but the print is smudged on like every other page near the spine, kinda hard to read some lines. also found a whole paragraph repeated twice on page 60 which was weird. story itself is decent so far i guess but the print quality is rough tbh.
bro the delivery guy just left my fiddle leaf fig leaning against the mailbox post in 95 degree heat for like six hours before i got home, half the leaves were basically fried by the time i found it.

I want to be fair and detailed about this yoga mat, because the marketing photos are a bit misleading: the surface texture shown up close in the listing suggested a grippy, slightly textured finish, but what I received is noticeably smoother and does become slippery within about fifteen minutes of a sweatier practice. The thickness measures accurately at six millimeters, and the color matches, but the traction claim in the description does not hold up under actual use.
succulent came in fine i guess but its like half the size of the one in the pics and the pot color is more grey than the sage green shown, kinda meh.

Order notes:
- Requested drop-off window: 8-10am
- Actual drop-off: left at the neighboring building's loading dock, not our address
- Cold items (yogurt, salmon) sat unrefrigerated roughly 4 hours before we located the bag
Package arrived on the promised date, no issues there. The problem is the stitching along the left cuff, which came undone after two washes.

The bonsai itself appears healthy, well-rooted and handsomely potted; regrettably, the courier left it at the address of a house three doors down, where it sat in direct sun for two days before the neighbor thought to inform me.

Before buying, I was afraid maybe the wood color will not match photo, this happen to me one time before with other website. But this was not problem, the color is same like picture, very nice. The real problem is the delivery man bring the table to wrong building in my complex, and it stay there three days on someone else porch before my neighbor tell me, and by that time one box get wet from rain and corner was soft.
the earbuds sound fine but the left one just randomly disconnects every few minutes, super annoying ngl. def a hardware thing not me.

I want to explain what happen with my winter coat order, is a little long story but I think important for other buyers to know. I order size L coat on 3 March, website say arrive in 5-7 days normally. First three days everything look normal, tracking say 'in transit.' Then tracking stop updating for entire week, no new scan, nothing. I email the company two times, they say wait few more days. On day 12 I check tracking again and now it say package is in different city, four hours drive from where I live, sitting at a sorting place. I do not understand why coat travel there when my address is not near that city at all. Day 15, tracking suddenly say 'out for delivery' but nothing come that day. Day 16 same message again, still nothing come to my door, I wait at home whole day for nothing. Finally on day 18 a driver from different courier company (not the one on original label) bring box to me, very confuse man, he say the label got attach to wrong truck at the hub. When I finally open the coat, it is exactly the color and size I want, very warm and good stitching, no problem with coat itself at all. But eighteen days for something that should take one week, plus wrong city, plus two days waiting for nothing, this was really frustrating experience and I almost cancel order before it come.

I confess I very nearly cancelled this order altogether. The parcel, containing a replacement kettle element, was consigned to a courier who saw fit to leave it propped against next door's gate rather than my own, and there it remained, unbeknownst to either household, for the better part of a week until the neighbour's gardener discovered it while trimming the hedge.
bread was stale already, tasted like it sat on a shelf for a week, wont buy this brand again

Can we just talk about how fast this got here?? Ordered on a Tuesday and it was on my porch by Thursday morning, super impressive turnaround! Unfortunately the actual toy robot doesn't hold up to the hype — the arm motor stalls out after about ten minutes of play and makes this awful grinding noise. Sent a video to support already. Speedy shipping, disappointing gadget.
the charger cable work but only if i hold it at specific angle, otherwise it stop charging my phone, think the wire is bad inside.

So this puzzle set looked adorable in the photos, and honestly the box art is still cute, but three of the pieces are warped just enough that they won't sit flush with the others, which is driving my daughter a little nuts. We've tried pressing them flat under some books for a few days and it's helped a tiny bit but not completely. Cute design, just wish the pieces themselves were made a bit sturdier.

The sound quality of these headphones exceeds anything I have previously owned; alas, the courier's own records show the parcel signed for at an address two streets from mine, and a fortnight passed before it was located.

Funny enough, I spent the whole week before this arrived convinced it would get stuck at customs the way my last overseas order did, dragging on for a month with no updates — my cousin still teases me about that one. This time, though, it showed up right on the day the tracking predicted, no drama at all. The only thing I'd note is that the cover art looked slightly more muted in person than on screen, but that's a printing thing, not really a complaint.

No, before you ask, the box wasn't late, wasn't lost, didn't show up dented — it appeared right on the doorstep exactly when the app said it would, practically suspicious in its punctuality. The actual letdown was cracking open the crate to find half the avocados already brown and mushy inside, which I can only assume is a quality control problem on the packing end, not anything that happened en route.
The paint on this action figure chips within a day of normal handling. Not durable enough for regular play.

I must commend the punctuality of the delivery; the parcel appeared on my doorstep a full two days ahead of the estimated date, neatly packaged and entirely undamaged. My praise, however, ends there, for the radio itself emits a persistent hum whenever the volume exceeds half its range, a defect I am reliably informed stems from a poorly shielded internal component rather than any mishandling along the way.

Concerns before ordering:
- Worried perishables might sit at a hub over the weekend
Actual outcome:
- Arrived next day as scheduled, all items still cold
- Only issue: the granola was slightly stale, likely close to its date
Nothing's wrong with the racket itself — strings taut, grip fine, frame straight. What's wrong is it sat in a regional depot two weeks while tracking cheerfully insisted 'out for delivery' daily.

To be clear: the shipment was not delayed, not misrouted, and arrived within the originally quoted window. The defect is internal to the product — page 214 is printed upside down relative to the rest of the signature.

Let me walk through the timeline in full, since I think it's relevant context: the order confirmation quoted an estimate of five business days, which felt reasonable for a paperback shipped domestically, and for the first four days the tracking updated normally, moving through two intermediate facilities as expected. On day five, however, the tracking simply stopped, no scans, no updates, nothing, and it stayed frozen in that state for an additional eleven days before a single new scan appeared showing the book had, for reasons never explained, been routed to a center in a different state entirely before finally correcting course and reaching my mailbox sixteen days after the original estimate.
The fern, upon closer inspection, harbours a small colony of aphids along the underside of its fronds, a detail conspicuously absent from the listing's description.
Upon unwrapping the golf bag, I discovered the zipper pull already detached from its slider — clearly a manufacturing slip, given how flimsy the stitching around it looks.

I regret to report that this order did not arrive within the fortnight originally promised. Indeed, three full weeks elapsed before anything appeared, and only after two telephone calls to the seller's office did the parcel finally turn up on my doorstep, rather battered along one corner as though it had been dropped from some height during its travels. The book inside was thankfully unharmed, but the whole affair tried my patience considerably.

I want to give a full account of this order because I think future buyers deserve the complete picture. I purchased three items together — a wool coat, a pair of gloves, and a scarf — all part of the same checkout and, according to the confirmation email, all sent in a single box via the seller's preferred carrier. The gloves and scarf arrived within the promised four-day window, neatly packaged in tissue paper, and both are lovely; no complaints there whatsoever. The coat, however, was apparently separated from the rest of the shipment at some point, because it never appeared in that first box at all. When I contacted support, they informed me that the carrier's manifest showed the coat as a separate parcel that had, in their words, 'gone missing in the network,' and that a trace request would take five to seven business days to resolve. Two weeks passed with no updates, so I called again, and only then did the seller agree to send a replacement coat at no additional charge, this time via a different carrier entirely. That replacement arrived six days later in perfect condition. In total, from the original order date to finally having the complete set of three items in hand, twenty-six days elapsed, twenty-two of which were spent waiting on a coat that had simply vanished somewhere between the warehouse and my house. I want to stress that the garments themselves, once I actually had them, were exactly as described and beautifully made. My frustration is entirely with how long it took, and how little visibility I had, to get the missing piece sorted out.
bro my dumbbells got lost for literally two weeks somewhere in transit and customer service kept giving me different answers every time i called lol.
the resistance bands snapped the second time i used them, like barely any stretch and they just gave out, kinda sketchy quality tbh.

So I scheduled this grocery order for a Saturday morning pickup window because that's the only time I have free between soccer practice and literally everything else, and instead the confirmation email I got an hour later said it had already been left on our porch overnight, except our porch camera shows nobody came by at all, so I spent half of Saturday on the phone trying to figure out where exactly our groceries actually went while my kids ate cereal for lunch because there was nothing else in the house.

ordered a case of sparkling water and it never showed up. tracking says delivered but theres nothing on my step, not even a dent in the grass where a box mightve sat. checked with neighbors on both sides and nobody has it either. this is the second time this month a package from this seller has just vanished like that.

So this is a bit of a saga, but bear with me because I think it's worth telling in full. My grandmother used to grow a fig tree in her backyard back in Ohio, and ever since she passed I've wanted one of my own, so when I finally found this listing I got a little sentimental about the whole thing and ordered it without thinking too hard about logistics. Big mistake, as it turns out. The tree was supposed to arrive within a week, which made sense to me since live plants shouldn't really sit around anywhere for long. Instead, the tracking page showed it sitting at an unnamed 'regional hub' for four days with zero movement, right in the middle of a heat wave, which had me picturing the poor thing basically baking inside a truck somewhere. When it finally did move again, the driver apparently couldn't find our unit number in the apartment complex and left it propped against the wrong building's fence, where it sat for almost two full days before a neighbor I've never even met knocked on my door holding it and asking if it was mine. By the time I actually got my hands on it, close to two weeks had passed since I placed the order, and the poor sapling looked stressed, with several yellowed leaves and soil that had clearly dried out completely at some point along the way. It's since perked up with some regular watering and a shadier spot on the balcony, so I think it'll pull through, but that whole business made me tear up a little, thinking about my grandmother's tree and how differently this one started its life with us.

The remote control car's steering only responds to left turns; the right-turn function does not engage at all, regardless of battery charge or distance from the receiver. Both wheels on the right side appear correctly attached, so the fault seems to be in the internal circuit board rather than assembly.
my package got sent to some warehouse in the wrong state and then just sat there for like 10 days before anyone noticed, absolute mess.
the crib's side rail bracket came out of the box already cracked, right where the screw hole is, and now im nervous to even use it for the baby without ordering a replacement part first.
The recliner's footrest mechanism jams halfway through reclining. This is a manufacturing fault, not related to assembly.

So I bought this dress for my cousin's wedding back in April — different wedding, long story, we have a lot of them in my family — and it's a gorgeous color in person, exactly like the swatch, but I noticed after about an hour of wear that the zipper on the side kept sliding down on its own no matter how I adjusted it, which was mortifying at the reception when my aunt had to help me fix it in the bathroom twice.

The toy kitchen set arrived nineteen days after the estimated delivery date. Tracking showed no movement for the first twelve days, then indicated the package had been rerouted through a facility in a neighboring state before finally reaching our address. Customer service could not explain the rerouting when contacted. The set itself was undamaged and complete once opened.
Ordered eggs and milk for same-day pickup; picked it up two days later after three separate calls, by which point I'd already bought replacements at the corner store out of sheer distrust.

Let me start by saying the plant itself, near as I can tell from the sad state it arrived in, would probably have been gorgeous under normal circumstances — nothing wrong with the variety, nothing wrong with how it was potted at the nursery, no complaints there at all, and I want to be fair about that part. The trouble is everything that happened to it after it left the nursery and before it reached my hands. I'd ordered this calathea as a surprise for my roommate's birthday, timed carefully so it would show up the Thursday before her party on Saturday, giving us a nice buffer. Thursday came and went with no delivery. Friday, the tracking page cheerfully claimed it was 'out for delivery,' a phrase which apparently means nothing at all in this company's internal language, because nothing arrived that day either. I called Friday evening in something of a panic, and was told, unhelpfully, that the driver had 'run out of time' on the route and the plant would simply try again Monday. Monday came, the party a distant memory by then, and still nothing showed. It wasn't until Tuesday — five days after the original estimate, and three days after the event it was meant for — that a driver finally left the box on our step, at which point I discovered the leaves inside had gone limp and several had yellowed, almost certainly from sitting boxed up somewhere without light or water through an entire weekend of transit delays. So to be clear: no issue with the plant they selected, no issue with how it was packaged at the source. The entire disappointment traces back to a shipment that took nearly a week to travel what should have been an overnight hop across town.
